doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Spike Jones and Louis Armstrong as live heroes
summary: He explains his Exeter nickname Spike, his Spike Jones records, and seeing the band at Symphony Hall.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Absolutely. Spike Jones was, believe it or not my nickname at Phillips Exeter was “Spike” and it was because of Spike Jones. I had every Spike Jones record made ever. Oh man. I mean I even had a Spike Jones band with the — and I borrowed the pistol from the athletic department [scats]. [Sings] You always hurt/the one —
Those guys could play though, man.

Oh could they ever. I saw every Spike Jones — if there were two musicians I would be there at some point if they were within 200 miles of me, those two are Louis Armstrong and the other was Spike Jones. I went to — every year he would come and pack Symphony Hall which holds 4,500 people, two shows a day and it was the funniest stuff you ever heard. You know the things that I learned from Spike Jones is, as you said, those guys were some of the best musicians in the world. George Brock the trumpet player and I can’t remember that drummer but the drummer was phenomenal. But they all were amazing. And the timing of all of the noises, the grunts and all, you know what I mean? It was dead on. Never miss. It was like listening to Buddy Rich.
